citations.claim: The accepted plan requires lease-based framework inventory and explicitly prohibits path-based Git snapshot discovery as a production or test entry point.
The concrete module publicly exposes both the required committed-snapshot lease operation and a parallel string-path operation.
The public string-path detailed operation invokes the alternate working-copy implementation without requiring or verifying an ICommittedRepositorySnapshotLease.
The framework test suite still discovers and invokes the public string-path operation by reflection, preserving the bypass as a test entry point.

constitution_must_relationship.details: No Constitution MUST is directly violated. The candidate remains reserved because the public alternate interface is a HIGH architecture-invariant and testability failure and a Strong recommendation; it also contradicts the accepted Story 4.3 remediation plan.

evidence: The production coordinator correctly supplies the same ICommittedRepositorySnapshotLease to framework and communication detection and verifies it again before the composite commit.
The lease-based detector verifies identity before and after reading the archive-only RootPath, and archive-only regression tests cover successful reads, mutation failure, and disposed-lease failure.
FrameworkEvidenceDetector nevertheless exposes parallel public overloads taking string workingCopyPath and routes them through independent Git inventory and blob reads.
FrameworkDetectionTests still locate and invoke the string-path operations by reflection, so the production lease interface is not the principal test surface.
The accepted remediation plan explicitly states that path-based Git snapshot discovery is not a production or test entry point.
candidates.problem: The framework detector module now supports the verified committed Repository snapshot lease used by production, but it simultaneously retains public string-path detection operations. Those operations construct a separate Git-derived snapshot and are still the dominant test entry point through reflection. Consequently, the module interface does not require ICommittedRepositorySnapshotLease, and tests can bypass the exact archive-only, before-and-after identity-verification seam that the accepted remediation says must be the sole production and test entry point.
candidates.solution: Remove the public string-path detection operations and the alternate Git snapshot-source path from the production module. Make tests acquire an ICommittedRepositorySnapshotLease and exercise IFrameworkEvidenceDetector, while keeping any parser-focused seams internal to the implementation. Add a public-interface contract test proving every inventory operation requires the committed snapshot lease.
candidates.title: Remove the parallel path-based framework detector interface

structured_result.exploration_summary: REVISE. Two former reserved blockers are fully cleared: every public RepositoryProfilingCoordinator constructor requires both the committed snapshot and Pre-Scan detector interfaces with no empty or missing adapter, and IScanRunRepository exposes only the composite RepositoryProfileCommitDraft persistence operation whose implementation transactionally commits profile data and the Pre-Scan Result with rollback and replay coverage. Production framework profiling also now uses and verifies an archive-only ICommittedRepositorySnapshotLease. One reserved finding remains: the concrete framework detector retains public string-path operations, backed by an alternate Git snapshot implementation, and the legacy framework suite still uses that interface. This contradicts the accepted remediation constraint, leaves revision semantics split across two interfaces, and preserves the test seam that allowed the original production mismatch to escape. No other CRITICAL/HIGH, Constitution MUST, Strong, or ADR-conflict finding was observed across integrated Epic 4; non-reserved catalog-locality debt was excluded.
